cards.title: Bench seep comparison notes

cards.title: Dark spot in snowpack: late winter photograph
cards.notes: Photograph of late-winter snowfield showing dark oval of upwelling wet ground; snow otherwise unbroken.

cards.title: Ice formation at emergence: photograph
cards.notes: Photograph of ice dome structure built up at spring emergence through successive winter nights.

cards.title: Groundwater level interpretation notes
cards.notes: Brief technical notes interpreting spring discharge as indicator of till reservoir condition across watershed.

cards.title: Adjacent seep comparison: slope distribution notes
cards.notes: Notes locating and describing other bench seep positions for comparison; this spring's persistence distinguished.

cards.title: Seasonal arrival record: first new growth at spring
cards.notes: Notes on first green emergence at spring zone compared to surrounding bench forest; temporal lead noted.

cards.notes: Brief notation of spring location as bench position reference in a traverse survey.

cards.title: Path wear record: approach from bench traverse
cards.notes: Notes on path condition from traverse to spring margin; wear evidence indicating repeated use.

cards.title: Crossing conditions calendar
cards.notes: Seasonal notation of when ford is passable, when ice can bear weight, and spring flood window.

cards.title: Weather observation log: temperature, pressure, wind, cloud
cards.notes: Multi-column weather log kept at ridge position; columns for temperature, cloud type, wind direction and force, barometer.

cards.title: Visibility record: long-range sightlines
cards.notes: Notes on visibility range under different atmospheric conditions; named structural features checked off by legibility.

cards.title: Fog ceiling height log: autumn mornings
cards.notes: Estimated fog ceiling height in autumn; compared to interior ridge profile to assess inversion depth.

cards.title: Barometric pressure record: weather event correlations
cards.notes: Pressure readings at ridge with subsequent weather noted; pattern recognition over multiple seasons.

cards.title: Wind direction frequency record: seasonal summary
cards.notes: Tally of wind directions at ridge position; winter northwest dominance vs. summer southwest noted.

cards.title: Cloud type identification notes
cards.notes: Handwritten notes on cloud identification from ridge; approach weather systems characterized by cloud type.

cards.title: Incoming weather approach: southwest horizon notes
cards.notes: Notes on reading incoming weather from southwest horizon before valley feels any change; lead time estimated.

cards.title: Valley fog from above: photograph
cards.notes: Photograph looking down from ridge into valley fog layer; interior ridge line projects above white surface.

cards.title: Clearing event sequence: atmospheric photograph
cards.notes: Photograph taken during post-frontal clearing: ridge in sunlight, valley still in cloud, transition zone moving down.

cards.title: Snow depth record at ridge
cards.notes: Seasonal snow depth at ridge bedrock vs. adjacent krummholz mat; wind scour effect documented.

cards.title: Phenology record: ice-in and ice-out dates
cards.notes: Annual record of first ice formation and last ice date at confluence, both channels noted separately.

cards.title: First and last snow date across years
cards.notes: Annual record of first snow at ridge vs. first snow at valley floor; ridge consistently first and last.

cards.title: Shelter maintenance log
cards.notes: Brief maintenance notes for ridge shelter: repairs made, condition of anchoring, weathering observations.

cards.title: Ridge approach condition notes: seasonal accessibility
cards.notes: Notes on when krummholz approach is passable; ice glaze conditions, deep-winter inaccessibility periods.

cards.title: Structural watershed sketch: drainage reading from overlook
cards.notes: Annotated sketch of the watershed as seen from ridge; tonal features identified, valley direction noted.

cards.title: Sunrise and sunset timing record: seasonal
cards.notes: Seasonal sunrise/sunset times recorded from ridge position; horizon obstruction by adjacent high point noted.

cards.title: Interior ridge above fog: photograph
cards.notes: Photograph showing interior secondary ridge projecting above valley fog layer; eastern drainage fog-free.

cards.title: Orientation diagram: watershed features as seen from ridge
cards.notes: Hand-drawn panoramic diagram annotating tonal features visible from ridge: valley band, interior ridge, lower wetland.

cards.title: Winter visibility conditions: post-frontal clarity notes
cards.notes: Notes on exceptional winter visibility after cold-front passage; named structural features legible.

cards.title: Rebecca's garden sketches
cards.notes: A page of sketches -- flowers, butterflies and ladybugs -- done by a 10-year-old Rebecca made from observations in her family's garden.

cards.title: Topographic survey excerpt: lower confluence terrain
cards.notes: Cropped section of a larger topographic survey showing the flat alluvial zone and tributary junction.

cards.title: Cold-air pooling temperature notes: autumn
cards.notes: Handwritten temperature comparisons: meadow vs. slope above, taken at dawn over several autumn mornings.

cards.title: Winter wildlife track documentation
cards.notes: Photographs of track sequences on snow-covered meadow, showing convergence from three corridor directions.

cards.title: Wet meadow vegetation survey
cards.notes: Species list for flood-maintained wet meadow, with notes on old channel depression community.

cards.title: Flood debris line photograph
cards.notes: Photograph of post-flood debris deposited at meadow margin, with rough high-water elevation notation.

cards.title: Eastern tributary response notes: post-rain
cards.notes: Field notes comparing how quickly eastern tributary rises after rainfall versus main channel.

cards.title: Fog occurrence log: confluence autumn mornings
cards.notes: Notebook page logging fog presence, density, and duration on autumn mornings at confluence.

cards.title: Survey stake inventory and coordinate notation
cards.notes: Typed list of boundary stakes with coordinate notes and condition assessment.

cards.title: Harvest tally sheets: row-by-row counts
cards.notes: Handwritten harvest tally sheets listing each tree row, bushels counted, and remarks on condition.

cards.title: Spray schedule: typed, seasonal
cards.notes: Typed spray application schedule listing material, dilution, and dates for each seasonal pass.

cards.title: Wildflower study: wet meadow species
cards.notes: Watercolor studies of five wet-meadow forbs; each plant shown in flower with a pressed specimen alongside. Painted in the field; color notes written in margin where pigment ran short.

cards.title: Color slide: spring flood at confluence
cards.notes: Kodachrome slide showing the confluence at spring flood peak; brown water carrying ice fragments, far bank submerged to lower branches. Sky a pale cold blue.

cards.title: Polaroid: autumn sedge margin
cards.notes: Faded Polaroid of the sedge margin in October; warm amber against standing water reflecting a grey sky. Print slightly overexposed at center.

cards.title: Nature journal page: frogs and herons
cards.notes: Child's journal page with pencil sketches of a green frog and a great blue heron, labeled in careful printing. A pressed cattail leaf taped to the bottom edge, now dried flat and pale.

cards.title: Pruning notes: tree condition observations
cards.notes: Handwritten notes on individual tree pruning decisions; notes on dead limbs, graft condition, shape.

cards.title: Postcard: confluence valley view
cards.notes: Printed postcard showing the valley corridor from an elevated vantage; colors hand-tinted, sky lavender-blue, meadow a saturated green. No message on reverse.

cards.title: Seed catalog page: apple varieties
cards.notes: Single page from a regional nursery catalog showing six apple varieties in color illustration: McIntosh, Northern Spy, Wealthy, and three now-obscure names. Colors slightly garish; the Wealthy is a deep arterial red.

cards.title: Harvest ribbon: county fair, apple class
cards.notes: Second-place ribbon in deep blue and gold; printed with county name and year. Attached by a small pin that has left a rust mark on the fabric. Apple class lettered in gilt.

cards.title: Painted crate label: variety name and orchard
cards.notes: Color-printed paper crate label with orchard name in bold serif type; apple illustration in red and green against a cream field. A faint blue border, slightly misregistered at one corner.

cards.title: Color slide: orchard at full blossom
cards.notes: Kodachrome slide of the orchard clearing at peak blossom; white and pale pink bloom against the dark spruce wall at the clearing edge. Sky an oversaturated Kodachrome blue.

cards.title: Orchard variety chart: hand-colored
cards.notes: Hand-drawn grid showing each row, variety, and rootstock; variety names written in ink, each column headed with a small watercolor patch in approximate fruit color. Annotations added over multiple seasons in different hands.

cards.title: Feed store advertisement: orchard spraying equipment
cards.notes: Printed broadsheet advertising a regional feed and farm supply store; orchard spray rigs illustrated in line engraving. A handwritten note in the margin: "ask about the 40-gal."

cards.title: Color slide: fruit accumulation on clearing floor
cards.notes: Slide showing windfallen apples covering the clearing floor in October; red and yellow against dark earth, some already browning. A deer track visible in the lower right corner.

cards.title: Mushroom sketches: forest floor species
cards.notes: Notebook page with watercolor sketches of four mushroom species found near the crossing; one identified by common name only, one with a question mark. Spore print glued alongside, rust-brown on white paper.

cards.title: Color slide: crossing in peak autumn
cards.notes: Kodachrome slide of the stone crossing in mid-October; yellow birch leaves banked against the upstream stones, water black in shadow. The flat above crossing visible and bright.

cards.title: Grafting diagram: variety layout
cards.notes: Hand-drawn diagram showing which variety was grafted to which rootstock position in the orchard.

cards.title: Camp pennant: watershed trail organization
cards.notes: Wool felt pennant in dark green with cream lettering; organization name and a stylized pine tree. Slightly moth-damaged at one edge. The kind issued for trail membership or canoe route completion.

cards.title: Painted trail marker: close-up photograph
cards.notes: Close-up photograph of a blaze on a birch trunk near the crossing approach; paint orange, applied in two coats, lower coat older and greyed. Bark has grown slightly around the older mark.

cards.title: Bird migration chart: waterfowl, eastern flyway
cards.notes: Hand-colored chart showing migration timing for nine waterfowl species; arrival and departure bars filled in watercolor by species. Duck silhouettes printed in black; color added in pencil and wash over multiple seasons.

cards.title: Color slide: waterfowl on open pond
cards.notes: Kodachrome slide of the pond in early May; a small group of ring-necked ducks on the water surface, standing dead behind them silver-white. Ice remnant at far margin.

cards.title: Insect collection card: dragonfly species
cards.notes: Mounting card with three pinned dragonfly specimens from the pond margin; species labels in small type below each. Wings intact and iridescent; one specimen slightly faded to amber.

cards.title: Color snapshot: autumn colors at pond
cards.notes: Early color snapshot — slightly warm-shifted with age — showing the pond in mid-October; tamarack yellow and red maple reflected in still water. A handwritten date on the back.

cards.title: Pressed sedge specimen: emergent species
cards.notes: Pressed and mounted sedge from the pond margin, glued to a notebook page with a penciled identification note. Stem flat and pale, seed head still intact.

cards.title: Watercolor geological section: bench stratigraphy
cards.notes: Hand-drawn cross-section of the western bench stratigraphy; layers colored in watercolor wash — buff for till, grey-brown for organic layer, pale yellow for sand lens. Prepared for a regional survey; field notations in pencil below the finished color.

cards.title: Child's handmade map: clearing and surrounding forest
cards.notes: Hand-drawn on ruled notebook paper in pencil and crayon; the stone foundation labeled 'old house,' the trail in red, the forest in green scribble. A north arrow pointing roughly northeast. Distances labeled in minutes of walking.

cards.title: Pressed flower collection: clearing species
cards.notes: Small envelope containing four pressed flowers from the clearing interior; goldenrod, a hawkweed, something in the aster family. Colors faded to cream and pale ochre. No labels, but the envelope is initialed.

cards.title: Row numbering system: pencil sketch
cards.notes: Schematic pencil sketch of orchard showing numbered rows and spacing, with margin annotations.

cards.title: Color slide: clearing at peak autumn color
cards.notes: Kodachrome slide of the clearing in October; pioneer birch and aspen in full yellow, foundation stone grey beneath. The contrast between the lit clearing and the dark spruce margin is pronounced in the slide.

cards.title: Naturalist notebook: spring wildflowers
cards.notes: Two notebook pages of watercolor field sketches: marsh marigold in vivid yellow, blue violet, early trout lily. Each plant labeled in a neat hand; color applied quickly, still wet when the page was turned — faint ghost print on facing page.

cards.title: Vegetation community diagram: spring zone
cards.notes: Hand-colored diagram showing plant community zones radiating from the spring emergence point; each zone labeled and colored in watercolor wash. Sphagnum in pale green, horsetail in grey-green, upland transition in buff.

cards.title: Color slide: spring zone in early June
cards.notes: Kodachrome slide of the spring emergence zone at peak early-summer color; marsh marigold still in flower at margin, new growth vivid against the still-bare mineral soil around the pool.

cards.title: Polaroid: spring emergence pool
cards.notes: Polaroid of the emergence pool in summer; water surface clear, sandy upwelling point visible at bottom. Print slightly warm-shifted. The scale of the pool is difficult to read without context.

cards.title: Hand-colored survey map: watershed overview
cards.notes: Printed survey base map with hand-applied color washes; watershed boundary in red, drainage network in blue ink, forest cover in a pale green wash that has faded unevenly. Elevation contours in printed black.

cards.title: Color slide: autumn valley from ridge
cards.notes: Kodachrome slide, autumn 1954. Valley corridor in full color. Deciduous band along valley floor orange, red, and gold. Surrounding slopes dark spruce-green. Sky slightly overexposed. Fine dust specks and a faint projection scratch. At the bottom edge of the frame, just visible, the blurred crown of another person’s head intrudes into the picture.

cards.title: Local fair program: watershed community
cards.notes: Folded paper program for an annual local fair; schedule of events includes agricultural classes, pie judging, and a "nature walk" entry. Printed in two colors — black and a dark red. One page detached.

cards.title: Watercolor sketch: ridge view with cloud shadow
cards.notes: Small watercolor sketch made from the overlook; valley rendered in loose washes of grey-green and ochre, a cloud shadow crossing the middle distance in blue-grey. The ridge foreground left unpainted — white paper.

cards.title: Bird migration chart: ridge hawk count
cards.notes: Hand-colored chart recording daily hawk counts at the ridge over six autumn seasons; broad-winged hawk peak marked with a vertical red line. Columns for species, wind direction, temperature. A good day circled in pencil.

cards.title: Apple variety list: handwritten inventory
cards.notes: Handwritten list of apple varieties present, with brief notes on production and hardiness.

cards.title: Incomplete Orchard Management Map
cards.notes: A tattered hand-drawn map with plans for re-grafting, clearing brush, replacing dead trees, repairing stone walls. Half the proposed work is checked off, half is unfinished, according to the record.

cards.title: Salvage inventory
cards.notes: A handwritten list made after the house was no longer occupied: kitchen stove removed, south window sash removed, roofing tin salvaged, pump handle removed.

cards.title: Browse line measurement record
cards.notes: Seasonal height measurements of browse line on orchard trees, year-over-year comparison.

cards.title: Phenology log: blossom dates and frost records
cards.notes: Annual log of first blossom date, last frost date, and harvest window start.

cards.title: Weather observation notebook: growing season
cards.notes: Daily weather notes from productive growing seasons: temperature, precipitation, frost events.

cards.title: Equipment maintenance log: ladders and sprayer
cards.notes: Record of ladder and spray equipment condition, repairs made, and replacement parts sourced.

cards.title: Bench seep output notation
cards.notes: Notes on seep flow above clearing: spring volume vs. late-summer minimum, and dry-year comparison.

cards.title: Succession margin advance measurements
cards.notes: Distances from known reference points to advancing pioneer shrub and birch margins, over several years.

cards.title: Drainage cut profile sketch
cards.notes: Cross-section sketch of the upslope drainage cut above orchard clearing, showing current condition.

cards.title: Orchard photograph: blossom period
cards.notes: Photograph of orchard clearing during blossom period; pale bloom visible against adjacent canopy. A second close-up photo of a blossom is stuck to it.

cards.title: Orchard photograph: autumn fruit accumulation
cards.notes: Photograph of fallen fruit accumulated on clearing floor in October; browse disturbance visible at margin.

cards.title: Fog below orchard: valley fog documentation
cards.notes: Photograph taken from orchard clearing looking downslope into valley fog filling lower corridor.

cards.title: Confluence channel geometry sketch
cards.notes: Hand-drawn plan of the confluence showing both channels and gravel bar positions at low water.

cards.title: Cider production notes
cards.notes: Handwritten notes on cider production quantities; apple source and yield from particular rows noted.

cards.title: Property boundary document: bench parcel
cards.notes: Fragment of boundary description document for the bench parcel; metes and bounds language.

cards.title: Winter orchard snow structure photograph
cards.notes: Photograph of clearing in winter; snow defines orchard spacing against surrounding unorganized forest.

cards.title: Stream stage measurement log: crossing point
cards.notes: Seasonal water level readings at crossing; notes on stone submersion depth at different flow states.

cards.title: Stone footing maintenance record
cards.notes: Notes on stone placement and adjustment; the gap between second and third stone noted with no action taken.

cards.title: Sound map: confluence on a June morning
cards.notes: Hand-drawn plan of the confluence area annotated with directional sound sources: frog chorus bearing south, water arriving audibly from two different directions, red-winged blackbird from the alder margin. A note reads "eastern tributary louder this morning — rain two days ago." Compass rose in pencil at center.

cards.title: Catch log: spring run at confluence
cards.notes: Small spiral notebook recording fishing outings at the confluence. Columns: date, species, length, condition, kept or released. Some dates are crossed out with no entry and no explanation. The last dated page has a single fish recorded and no further pages filled.

cards.title: Trapping record: mink and muskrat sets
cards.notes: Pocket notebook listing trap set locations by number, species caught, date, and pelt condition. Inside front cover: a rough sketch map of the meadow with numbered trap positions in pencil. A note beside one set: "flooded out — moved to bank edge."

cards.title: Child's nature report: the frog pond
cards.notes: Three handwritten pages in careful printing recording observations at the wet meadow over a summer. Opening line: "I watched the frog pond six times." Pencil drawings of tadpoles and a great blue heron, labeled by name. Teacher comments in red at the margin: "very good observation." A grass stain across the back page.

cards.title: Photo series: confluence bank, four seasons
cards.notes: Four photographs taken from the same marked position on the east bank: spring flood, summer sedge, autumn color, winter ice. The marker stake is visible in three of the four frames. Season and year written in the same hand on the back of each print.

cards.title: Tool shed inventory: ladders, sprayer, and implements
cards.notes: Two handwritten pages listing the orchard shed contents: four ladders by length and condition, two spray tanks with capacities, pruning saws, picking hooks, a hand-cart noted as "wheel split — not replaced." Items struck through as lost or discarded; the list appears to have been amended across at least three seasons in different pencil densities.

cards.title: Recipe card: apple butter, orchard batch
cards.notes: Index card in faded blue ink: apple quantity, cider, spices, yield in quarts. A margin note reads "use the Wealthys, not the Spies." A penciled asterisk next to the reduction step with no accompanying explanation. Some spattering on the lower edge consistent with use near a heat source.

cards.title: Route map excerpt: western bench traverse
cards.notes: Cropped section of a larger route map showing crossing location in context of bench traverse network.

cards.title: Child's drawing: the orchard in blossom
cards.notes: Crayon on ruled school paper. Trees in white and pale pink against a blue sky; one tree labeled "the biggest one." A small figure with a ladder stands at the far margin. The figure has been erased and redrawn at least once — the ghost of the first attempt still visible below the crayon.

cards.title: Tin label: preserved apple, orchard name
cards.notes: Paper label removed from a preserved-fruit tin: orchard name in bold type, variety and pack year below. A small apple in line engraving. Water damage at one corner has blurred the pack year to near-illegibility. Edges torn unevenly where the label was peeled from the tin.

cards.title: Rubbing: stone wall inscription
cards.notes: Pencil rubbing on thin drafting paper taken from an inscription on the orchard boundary wall. A set of initials and what may be a year; partially legible, the stone surface texture transferring clearly around the carved lines. Mounted on backing paper with a brief annotation: "south wall, third panel."

cards.title: Leaf rubbing collection: approach corridor
cards.notes: Notebook of pencil rubbings gathered on the approach to the crossing: yellow birch, striped maple, hobblebush, and one labeled with a question mark. Colors have faded to grey but vein structure is distinct. The last page has a fern pressed alongside, dried flat and pale, held by a strip of tape that has yellowed.

cards.title: Growth ring count: felled spruce near crossing
cards.notes: Handwritten notes from counting rings on a spruce stump near the crossing: total rings, estimated year of germination, and a note on a compressed decade — narrow rings, no explanation offered. A pencil diagram of the stump cross-section shows the ring asymmetry: one side significantly wider than the other.

cards.title: Stone collection: nine from the crossing
cards.notes: A small cloth bag containing nine smooth stones selected from the stepping stones. Each labeled with a strip of paper tied with thread, numbered 1 through 9. A handwritten list names each: "flat grey," "the orange one," "the egg," "blue if wet," "heavy one." The bag is initialed on the inside seam.

cards.title: Photo series: same view at the crossing, four seasons
cards.notes: Four photographs taken from a marked position above the stepping stones, one per season. Stones fully exposed in late summer, submerged in spring; summer moss disappears under snow in winter. The water surface changes shape entirely between seasons. Year written on the back of each in the same hand.

cards.title: Mending record: pack trip gear across seasons
cards.notes: Small notebook tracking repairs to gear used on approaches through the crossing corridor: wool socks (right heel repaired three times, left heel once), a pack strap, a canvas waterproof pouch. The last sock entry: "not worth it again." A needle and a spool of thread tucked into the back cover.

cards.title: Soil sample card: pond margin core
cards.notes: Index card recording a hand-core taken at the pond margin: organic muck depth in centimeters, grey mineral layer below, compacted till beneath that. A note: "sulfide smell at depth." Sample position marked with a dot on a small sketch of the pond margin drawn in the card corner.

cards.title: Star observation log: from the beaver dam
cards.notes: Notebook pages recording observations made while sitting on the dam at night: planet positions in two seasons, Milky Way visibility, and one note: "three meteorites, northwest to southeast, approximately 11:40pm — could not sleep." Water reflections mentioned twice as part of what was seen.

cards.title: Seasonal access log: spring closure and re-opening
cards.notes: Annual notes on when spring flood makes crossing impassable and when stones re-emerge.

cards.title: Growth ring count: gnawed birch at dam margin
cards.notes: Notes from counting rings on a beaver-felled birch stub at the dam: total rings, estimated diameter at time of felling. A margin note compares this to the smallest-diameter birch previously recorded at the site. The stub was small enough to count by eye without sectioning.

cards.title: Child's diary entry: the dam
cards.notes: Two sentences in large, careful cursive on a half-page of ruled notebook paper: "Today we walked all the way to the beaver dam. I saw a red-winged blackbird and a dead tree with no bark." A date is attempted at the top but the year is smudged beyond reading.

cards.title: Decay documentation: same timber, four visits
cards.notes: Sketches and notes from four visits to the same fallen birch inside the impoundment zone; the log's progression from solid to soft to fragmented recorded across an estimated fifteen years. Fungi succession noted visit by visit: shelf fungi by the second visit, substrate collapsed at the fourth. The final entry estimates three more years of visible coherence.

cards.title: Child's rubbings: foundation stone surfaces
cards.notes: Four pencil rubbings on thin drafting paper taken from foundation stone surfaces. Lichen patterns, surface texture, and what may be a tool mark are visible on the third sheet. The fourth rubbing is smeared — paper shifted during transfer. Sheets labeled in the child's own shorthand: "corner," "long side," "back," "fell one."

cards.title: Growth ring count: pioneer birch in clearing interior
cards.notes: Notes on counting rings in a pioneer birch that fell inside the former foundation footprint. Working backward from the count to an estimated germination year, a penciled note: "if count is right, this tree came up within 10 years of abandonment." A second hand has added in the margin: "check against deed fragment."

cards.title: Mineral sample card: stones from the clearing floor
cards.notes: Small card with three fragments glued alongside pencil labels: red granite, pale feldspar, and flat grey shale. The shale entry notes: "doesn't match the foundation stone — not from here." Collected from the clearing floor surface, not from any structural course.

cards.title: Tool cache list: stone-setting implements
cards.notes: Fragment of a handwritten list from the construction period: stone bars, mallets, and wedges itemized with rough counts. One entry reads "chisel — at mill." The ink has faded to brown; the lower portion of the page is torn away, leaving the list incomplete.

cards.title: Decay documentation: fallen interior timber, four visits
cards.notes: Notes and rough sketches from four return visits to the same fallen log inside the former foundation footprint. Collapse progression recorded across what appears to be twelve to fifteen years; fungi names attempted in two entries, one crossed out and corrected. The final note estimates the wood will be gone into the substrate within three more years.

cards.title: Foraging notes: spring-adjacent plants
cards.notes: Pencil notes on edible and medicinal plants found near the spring emergence zone: watercress, ostrich fern fiddleheads, horsetail with a cautionary note on quantity. A rough sketch of each. A later hand has added a question mark next to the horsetail entry with no further comment.

cards.title: Water taste record: seasonal notes
cards.notes: Brief handwritten observations on the spring's taste across visits and years: "sharp and cold in February," "faintly of iron in June after a dry May," "clean and without character in late summer." A note at the bottom compares it favorably to a named well in the valley, which "had gone off."

cards.title: Blaze inventory: marked trees along approach
cards.notes: Record of blazed trees on approach routes to crossing; includes the healed cut on downstream spruce.

cards.title: Child's watercolor: the spring pool
cards.notes: Small watercolor painted at the site. The pool in three overlapping shades of blue-green; a yellow-green fern at the margin; bare mineral soil around the emergence point left as unpainted white paper. Paint muddied at the center where too much water was used. The paper has warped from field use.

cards.title: Sound log: spring zone, four seasons
cards.notes: Notebook pages recording what was audible at the spring across seasons: winter drip into ice and nothing else, spring wood thrush from the bench above, summer insect constant, autumn silence broken only by movement in leaf litter. A note on the winter page: "only the drip. Nothing else for twenty minutes."

cards.title: Photo series: emergence zone, five years
cards.notes: Five photographs taken from the same position above the pool, one each autumn. Year penciled on the back of each. Small year-on-year differences in pool margin and sphagnum extent visible on comparison; a birch sapling at the left edge grows measurably taller across the sequence.

cards.title: Star map: sky from the ridge
cards.notes: Hand-drawn map on dark paper, stars marked in white pencil; constellations labeled, Milky Way indicated by a shaded arc. A circled point carries a note: "this one moved — not a star." The ridge outline is drawn along the bottom edge for orientation. A planet is noted in the margin with an estimated month.

cards.title: Firewood record: ridge shelter fuel across winters
cards.notes: A pocket ledger recording fuel brought to the ridge shelter and consumed per stay: bundle counts or estimated weight, ambient temperature at arrival, overnight low. One entry: "green — poor." Another: "brought too much, left half — still there next time." The record spans eight winters.

cards.title: Radio reception log: ridge position vs. valley
cards.notes: Notes comparing signal quality at the ridge versus the valley floor. Stations listed with clarity ratings across seasons; a Montreal station noted as reliably clear in winter from the ridge, absent from the valley. A note: "try northwest side of shelter in summer — spruce blocks it now."

cards.title: Tool inventory: ridge shelter cache
cards.notes: A list of tools cached at the ridge shelter: a whetstone, a folding saw, two coils of spare rope, a tin of tallow, and three items listed as "missing." One entry reads "replaced — original gone." Written in at least three different hands; the list was clearly added to over years rather than recopied fresh.

cards.title: Sound map: ridge in high wind
cards.notes: Diagram of the ridge drawn from above, with sound sources annotated for a sustained northwest wind event: wind tone through krummholz mat (constant), ice tick on exposed bedrock (intermittent, northeast face), shelter line drumming (gusts only). A note at the bottom: "no valley sounds audible at all. Could hear my own breathing."

cards.title: Letter fragment: describing the view from the ridge
cards.notes: Half a page of a letter, torn across the top, no salutation surviving. The writer describes the view at length: the valley corridor, "the southern peaks which I take to be thirty miles," morning light on the opposite slope. The handwriting grows smaller toward the bottom as if a page end was approaching. No signature.

cards.notes: Excerpt from a regional hydrological study noting the beaver impoundment and downstream flow modification.

cards.title: Pond surface fog observation notes: autumn
cards.notes: Field notes on shallow surface fog at pond; onset conditions, height, and dissipation rate compared to valley fog.

cards.notes: Seasonal observations on pond water clarity; spring turbid, autumn clear; notes on sediment behavior near source.

cards.title: Passage record: seasonal crossing conditions at dam
cards.notes: Notes on seasonal passability of dam crossing: footing condition, water above dam in spring, ice in winter.

cards.title: B+W scan: stream with gravel bars, winter
cards.notes: Aged print with heavy edge damage and water staining. A stream winds through bare-branch winter landscape. Gravel banks exposed on both sides of a low-gradient channel. Mixed riparian vegetation: conifers behind, bare deciduous at the water margin. Flat alluvial terrain surrounds the channel. The stream width, exposed gravel, and alluvial character match the confluence zone at winter low water. File: TC-scan-001-stream-with-gravel-bars-winter.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: stream bend and alluvial banks
cards.notes: Companion to the gravel bar photograph, taken from a slightly different angle at the same location. Channel bends through flat terrain. Gravel and sediment banks visible. Bare deciduous trees with conifers at distance. Water level low, exposing the alluvial substrate. Same aging and edge damage as its pair. File: TC-scan-002-stream-bend-and-alluvial-banks.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: flat meadow toward distant structures
cards.notes: Flat, open grass or sedge field extending toward distant farmstead structures. Low overcast sky. Vegetation winter-dormant or early spring. The horizontal character dominates. No enclosing forest visible at the meadow surface. The structures in the middle ground read as habitation within the valley system, visible from the open flood-maintained meadow. File: TC-scan-003-flat-meadow-toward-distant-structures.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: flat sedge margin with young trees
cards.notes: Flat, low-lying terrain. Dry sedge or grass in the foreground. Young deciduous trees scattered across the middle ground in irregular colonization pattern. Conifer forest line at distance. Transitional character between open meadow and enclosing forest. Faded print with soft tonal range. The pioneer trees advancing from the forest edge match the alder-willow transition zone described at the meadow perimeter. File: TC-scan-004-flat-sedge-margin-with-young-trees.jpg

cards.title: Canal extent sketch: lateral drainage
cards.notes: Pencil sketch showing canal channels extending from pond margin into formerly dry valley-floor terrain.

cards.title: B+W scan: open ground and cumulus sky
cards.notes: Very flat, open landscape. Cumulus clouds dominate the upper two-thirds of the frame. Low vegetation at ground level. Transmission towers visible on the horizon. The flat openness and sky dominance carry atmospheric resonance with the confluence meadow's exposure to weather, though the scale exceeds the meadow. Contextual rather than site-specific. File: TC-scan-005-possible-open-meadow-and-sky.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: cultivated planting among conifers
cards.notes: Ornamental landscape: a weeping deciduous tree flanked by upright conifers. Daffodils at ground level. Maintained lawn. The formality exceeds what the orchard clearing would have shown, but the persistence of cultivated vegetation within a conifer framework carries atmospheric value. The deliberate arrangement of planted specimens among the surrounding forest evokes the orchard's managed legacy. File: AO-scan-001-possible-cultivated-planting-with-conifers.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: worked ground under canopy
cards.notes: Tilled or recently worked earth in an open clearing, framed by a large deciduous tree canopy overhead. Shrubby and forested margin at the far edge. The combination of altered soil, mature canopy shade, and forest pressing at the margins reads as the orchard clearing's cultivated character. The worked ground and the tree above it occupy the same spatial relationship as the orchard floor and its surviving canopy. File: AO-scan-002-worked-ground-under-canopy.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: spaced trees on hillslope
cards.notes: Small trees at semi-regular spacing on a grassy hillslope. Dry grass between them. Mountain or ridge rising in the background through haze. The moderate slope and the tree spacing, inconsistent with natural forest recruitment, read as intentional planting on bench-slope terrain. The environmental character matches the abandoned orchard precisely: persistence of managed spacing, open ground under succession, ridge backdrop above. One of the strongest site matches in the scan collection. File: AO-scan-003-spaced-trees-on-hillslope.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: orchard spacing on grassy hillside
cards.notes: Mature trees at wide, semi-regular intervals on a grassy hillside. The trees have the spreading canopy form of fruit or nut species rather than forest trees. Furrowed or textured ground surface. The orchard spacing is legible across the clearing. The tree arrangement, grassy intervals, and hillside position read as the abandoned orchard's described character. Companion to the hillslope scan. File: AO-scan-004-orchard-spacing-on-grassy-hillside.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: rocky stream through forested ravine
cards.notes: Stream flowing over rocks and boulders in a steep, forested ravine. Dense conifer canopy above. Water moving with energy through a confined, rocky channel. The enclosure is complete on both sides. The rocky substrate, confined channel width, and conifer-forested enclosure match the crossing's described physical structure: the seep-fed tributary cutting through glacial till on the western slope. File: FC-scan-001-rocky-stream-through-forested-ravine.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: steep drainage through conifers
cards.notes: Dated AUG 57 on the print. Large waterfall descending through dense conifer forest in a steep-sided ravine. Substantial water volume exceeding the crossing's described 1-2 meter stream width. The environmental character resonates with the ravine system's drainage energy even though the scale is wrong. Atmospheric rather than site-specific; the waterfall's relationship to the surrounding forest has archival value for depicting the drainage corridor's character under high-energy conditions. File: FC-scan-002-possible-steep-drainage-through-conifers.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: winter trail through snow woods
cards.notes: Dated MAR 56 on the print. Heavy snow on bare deciduous branches. A path or trail descends through enclosed winter woods. Stone or log features visible at ground level near the bottom of the frame. The enclosed character, the trail through mixed forest, and the ground-level features match the forest crossing's approach: the descent through bench forest toward the ravine head in late winter. File: FC-scan-003-winter-trail-through-snow-woods.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: winter ice at impoundment margin
cards.notes: Flat frozen surface. Three figures skating. Bare deciduous trees at left margin, dense conifer forest behind. Snow on banks. The flat expanse of ice bounded by forest on both sides suggests a frozen water body in a confined valley corridor. The human presence, people using the frozen surface, suggests the kind of seasonal access the impoundment would permit when winter freezes the pond solid. File: BM-scan-001-winter-ice-at-impoundment-margin.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: dense shrub margin in summer
cards.notes: Two figures immersed in extremely dense deciduous shrub growth. Multi-stemmed, tangled vegetation at and above head height. Full summer leaf. The density and multi-stemmed character are consistent with the vigorous willow and alder colonization at the impoundment's margins, the early-successional shrub establishing in light-rich, organically enriched conditions where forest formerly stood. The people provide scale for the vegetation height. File: BM-scan-002-possible-dense-shrub-margin-in-summer.jpg

cards.title: Spring flood high-water marks
cards.notes: Annual notations of flood extent on bank stake; comparison across years noted in margin.

cards.title: Standing dead in fog: photograph
cards.notes: Photograph of standing dead timber emerging through shallow autumn fog above pond surface.

cards.title: B+W scan: still water with young margin trees
cards.notes: Still water body with dense mixed forest behind. Young deciduous trees establishing at the water's edge. Flat water surface. The calm, contained quality of the water within a forested corridor matches the impoundment's character: open water backed by forest, with pioneer vegetation at the transitional margin. A utility pole is visible but does not dominate the composition. File: BM-scan-003-still-water-with-young-margin-trees.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: still water and reflected forest
cards.notes: Wide stream or river with a leaning deciduous tree extending over still water. Dense canopy reflected in the water surface. The reflection is detailed and continuous. The calm water reflecting surrounding forest canopy is one of the beaver meadow's most characteristic atmospheric signatures. The leaning and partially fallen trunk reads as the standing dead timber at the impoundment margin. Aged print with warm tonal shift. File: BM-scan-004-still-water-and-reflected-forest.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: stone steps and cultivated ground
cards.notes: Woman seated on stone steps in a garden setting. Vegetation growing around and over the stone, both cultivated and self-seeded. The stone construction is being incorporated into the surrounding growth. The combination of worked stone and advancing plant life echoes the stone foundation's defining condition: cultural residue being absorbed by ecological process. File: SF-scan-001-stone-steps-and-cultivated-ground.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: cabin among conifers
cards.notes: Woman on the porch of a shingled wood cabin. Mature conifers behind. Wicker furniture, vine-covered post, stone border at the base. The built structure among conifers represents the habitation condition that the stone foundation records in its aftermath: the organic structure that preceded the stone-only remnant. The stone border at the base echoes the surviving foundation courses. File: SF-scan-002-cabin-among-conifers.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: winter conifers and structure
cards.notes: Tall, straight conifer trunks in snow. A small structure or cabin visible at the right edge of the frame. Long shadows on the snow surface. The structure glimpsed through winter conifer forest reads as the bench forest condition: former habitation visible as a small presence within the larger forest matrix. The snow conditions make the clearing and the structure legible against the surrounding canopy. File: SF-scan-003-winter-conifers-and-structure.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: collapsing structure in overgrown field
cards.notes: Dilapidated wooden shed or outbuilding in advanced collapse. Overgrown field surrounds it. Bare deciduous trees at margins. Dry winter grass. The structure is losing its form to time and weather. The organic structure decomposes while the clearing it created persists, slowly narrowed by succession. This is the stone foundation clearing's central condition expressed through its earlier phase: a built presence returning to the ground. The strongest single-image evocation of reclamation in the scan collection. File: SF-scan-004-collapsing-structure-in-overgrown-field.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: clearing with succession from margins
cards.notes: Open grassy clearing on a hillside. Young trees and shrubs establishing from the margins. Forested hillside beyond. A gap through the trees reveals a view downslope toward distant terrain. The clearing is being actively compressed by advancing vegetation. The pioneer growth at the margins and the downslope gap match the stone foundation clearing's bench position, where succession presses inward and the valley floor is occasionally visible below. File: SF-scan-005-clearing-with-succession-from-margins.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: view through pines downslope
cards.notes: Dated APR 66 on the print. View through mature pine trunks downslope toward buildings and a road below. Dense understory shrubs. The perspective is from an elevated, forested position looking down. The spatial relationship, a bench position in the forest with the valley and its contents partly visible through gaps in the canopy, matches the described approach to the stone foundation clearing. April conditions suggest early spring before full leaf. File: SF-scan-006-possible-view-through-pines-downslope.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: enclosed verdant path
cards.notes: Dense vegetation enclosing a narrow path. Ferns, broad-leaved plants, overhanging canopy. Deeply enclosed with dappled light through thick cover. Moisture-rich character throughout. The vegetation is climate-incongruent with the watershed, but the environmental character resonates with the headwater spring: deep enclosure, intimate scale, proximity to saturated ground, dense ground-level growth, and the absence of any view beyond the immediate surroundings. Atmospheric rather than documentary. File: HS-scan-001-possible-enclosed-verdant-path.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: couple on exposed ridge grass
cards.notes: Two figures standing on an exposed grassy hilltop. Sky dominates the frame. Wind-moved grass. No trees in the immediate vicinity. The elevation and exposure are the primary conditions. Period estimated from clothing. The wind in the grass and the sky's dominance express the ridge position's defining qualities: exposure, height, and the absence of canopy. File: RO-scan-001-couple-on-exposed-ridge-grass.jpg

cards.title: Spring ice breakup: pond vs. channel
cards.notes: Photograph showing fractured pond ice and open tributary channel below dam; transitional ice state.

cards.title: B+W scan: conifer canopy toward distant ridge
cards.notes: View through conifer treetops toward a distant mountain or ridge partly obscured by haze. The viewer is at elevation, looking through the upper canopy toward terrain beyond. The transition zone on the ascent to the overlook: still within the conifer canopy but with the distant ridge beginning to appear through gaps. Scratches on the print surface. File: RO-scan-002-conifer-canopy-toward-distant-ridge.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: valley view from fenced hillside
cards.notes: Rolling pastoral landscape from an elevated position. Fenced fields, scattered pine trees, distant hills and ridges with forested slopes. Farm structures in the middle distance. The perspective reads the landscape as a system of relationships: foreground slope descending to valley floor, the floor extending toward distant terrain. The structural understanding of landscape-as-system matches the overlook's orientation function. File: RO-scan-003-valley-view-from-fenced-hillside.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: mountain valley from upper slope
cards.notes: Mountain valley viewed from high on a slope. Sparse young trees and scrub in the foreground. Ridges descending into the valley below. Cloud or fog partially obscuring a distant peak. The scrubby foreground vegetation, sparse trees on thin soil, and cloud-obscured ridge suggest the upper slope approach to the overlook position, near the krummholz transition zone. File: RO-scan-004-mountain-valley-from-upper-slope.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: valley and ridges from stone shelf
cards.notes: Panoramic valley view from elevation. Stone wall or bedrock shelf in the foreground. Lake or river in the middle distance. Layered mountains and ridges receding into atmospheric haze. The stone shelf echoes the exposed bedrock of the overlook position. The layered ridges, water corridor below, and atmospheric recession express exactly the structural visibility the ridge provides: the drainage system's logic readable from elevation. The strongest ridge match in the scan collection. File: RO-scan-005-valley-and-ridges-from-stone-shelf.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: flat horizon and sky
cards.notes: Flat landscape, large sky with cumulus clouds. Transmission towers on the horizon. The sky dominance and uninterrupted horizon carry atmospheric resonance with the ridge's exposure condition, though the terrain is flat rather than elevated. The big sky and distant horizon express what the overlook experiences from above. Contextual rather than site-specific. File: RO-scan-006-possible-flat-horizon-and-sky.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: exposed boulder among conifers
cards.notes: Large exposed boulder or rock outcrop with conifer forest behind. Bare ground around the rock. Clear sky visible above. Light-colored, weathered surface. The bedrock exposure among conifers matches the ridge's physical structure: the Precambrian gneiss shelf exposed by frost action and wind scouring, with surrounding conifers pressing close but unable to establish on the bare rock surface. File: RO-scan-007-exposed-boulder-among-conifers.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: valley view through conifers from height
cards.notes: View from elevation through large conifers into a deep valley. Distant mountains and ridges beyond. A waterfall or light-colored feature visible in the valley below. The structural reading from the ridge down into the valley: the drainage system visible as a corridor descending between forested slopes, distant ridges providing the containment arc. One of the strongest overlook matches. File: RO-scan-008-valley-view-through-conifers-from-height.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: high-elevation conifers with snow
cards.notes: High-elevation conifer forest with persistent snow patches. Ridgeline with exposed rock faces and dense spruce. Subalpine character. Snow persistence and rock exposure suggest elevation near or above the tree limit. The upper watershed environment where the ridge sheds its forest cover and exposes the underlying bedrock. File: RO-scan-009-high-elevation-conifers-with-snow.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: dead trunk at ridgetop with haze
cards.notes: Ridgetop or high slope. Dead standing trunk prominent and bare, projecting against the open sky. Dense low vegetation surrounding it. View below and beyond dissolves into atmospheric haze. The dead trunk at an exposed position, the view downward through haze, and the dense low vegetation suggest the krummholz transition zone at the upper tree limit. The wind-shaped character of the surrounding growth is legible. File: RO-scan-010-dead-trunk-at-ridgetop-with-haze.jpg

cards.title: B+W scan: ridge silhouette at dusk
cards.notes: Silhouette of a ridge and scattered trees against a dusk or dawn sky. Foreground in deep shadow. Ridge profile readable as a line against layered clouds. The ridge at the boundary between day and night. The silhouetted profile and scattered trees express the exposure condition and the relationship to the sky. Atmospheric rather than documentary, but carries the ridge position's defining visual quality: the horizon line, the sky above, the watershed below. File: RO-scan-011-ridge-silhouette-at-dusk.jpg

cards.title: Ash Light
cards.description: Flat grey light without identifiable source or direction. Color desaturates and the time of day is hard to read from the sky.

cards.title: Canopy Suppression
cards.description: Dense canopy holding light out. Dimness at midday. Ground vegetation thins to what tolerates shade, and the eye works close to the ground.

cards.title: Held Fog + Open Canopy + Ground Saturation
cards.description: Diffuse light, weak horizon, reflective wet ground under sparse branches. Forms emerge by proximity; detail resolves close while distance stays soft.

cards.title: Wind Exposure + Long Distance + Residual Cold
cards.description: Directional grass movement, broad horizons, cold light, distant weather visible. Little enclosure; most of what can be heard is wind, and surfaces stay colder than the air.

cards.title: Suppressed Distance + Dense Growth + Muted Sound
cards.description: Layered obstruction, absorbed sound, sightlines that end early. Movement guided by gaps and near detail; no position gives an overview.

cards.title: Low Water + Surface Reflection
cards.description: Shrunken channels lying still. Residual pools double the sky among exposed stone; the bed reads as rock with mirrors set into it.

cards.title: Residual Cold + Filtered Light
cards.description: Even, shadowless light over ground still hard in the shade. Frost persisting at midday under cloud.

cards.title: Weather Compression + Horizon Exposure
cards.description: Open terrain under a low cloud ceiling. Wide but not tall; the visible world extends outward, and arriving weather can be watched across the whole distance.

cards.title: Ground Saturation + Open Canopy
cards.description: Wet ground lit at depth through bare branches. Standing water carries the canopy's pattern downward, so the floor of the woods is doubled and brighter than the season suggests.

cards.title: Distant Brightness + Suppressed Distance
cards.description: Enclosed near ground with lit terrain showing through gaps; the close world stays dull while far ground carries the light.

cards.title: Wind Exposure + Surface Reflection
cards.description: Wind texturing open water. The sky's double broken into movement; reflection becomes intermittent, reassembling in lulls. The water shows the wind more clearly than the grass does.

cards.title: Deferred Visibility
cards.description: Conditions that seem about to clear and do not. Visibility fluctuates without resolving, opening and collapsing again.

cards.title: Dense Growth
cards.description: Vegetation thick enough to obstruct. Layered, irregular spacing; interrupted sightlines. Movement is guided by gaps, sound, and texture rather than clear pathing.

cards.title: Distant Brightness
cards.description: Light on far terrain while the near ground stays dull. A lit ridge, a pale band under cloud. Brightness located elsewhere.

cards.title: Filtered Light
cards.description: Light arriving through canopy, cloud, or haze. No direct shadow. Surfaces are evenly lit and shapes lose their modeling.

cards.title: Ground Saturation
cards.description: The ground holds water. Footing softens, low places stand wet, surfaces reflect. Every step makes sound.

cards.title: Held Fog
cards.description: Fog that does not lift or move. Near forms stay sharp while distance softens. Sound arrives close and damp.

cards.title: Horizon Exposure
cards.description: Terrain falls away on more than one side and the horizon becomes most of what is visible. Scale registers before detail does.

cards.title: Late Growth
cards.description: Vegetation past its peak and still growing. New shoots among collapsed stems. The season's order visibly mixed on the same ground.

cards.title: Long Distance
cards.description: Sightlines carrying past the local terrain to country beyond it. Far weather is visible before it arrives.

cards.title: Long Drainage
cards.description: Water audible or visible moving downslope over an extended distance. The terrain reads as a route even where there is no path.

cards.title: Low Water
cards.description: Channels below their banks. Exposed stone, dried margins, water lines on rock. The route of water visible without much of the water.

cards.title: Muted Sound
cards.description: The environment absorbs more than it returns. Footfalls shorten, distant sound does not arrive, and quiet reads as a property of the ground rather than an absence.

cards.title: Open Canopy
cards.description: Bare or sparse branches overhead. Light reaches the ground unevenly and the understory is visible at depth. The sky is present inside the woods.

cards.title: Residual Cold
cards.description: Cold remaining after its weather has gone. Shaded ground stays hard, ice persists where sun does not reach, and the air is warmer than the surfaces.

cards.title: Soft Horizon
cards.description: The line between land and sky does not resolve. Haze, light, or moisture blends them, and the far edge of the visible stays approximate.

cards.title: Suppressed Distance
cards.description: Sightlines end early. Vegetation, terrain, or weather closes every view within a short range. Overview is unavailable; the environment is understood incrementally.

cards.title: Surface Reflection
cards.description: Standing or slow water doubling the sky. Pale where the sky is pale, dark where it is dark. Depth unreadable.

cards.title: Uneven Warmth
cards.description: Warmth in patches: sun on one slope, cold air pooled below it. Crossing terrain means crossing temperatures.

cards.title: Weather Compression
cards.description: Weather close overhead. The cloud base sits low enough to flatten the vertical, and the sky participates in the enclosure.

cards.title: Wind Exposure
cards.description: Continuous wind across open ground. Grass lies in one direction, cloud shadows travel, and most of what can be heard is wind. Everything else has to get through it.
